It can be complicated.

Microsoft has a library of drivers that vendors make for their hardware, and have submitted to Microsoft for certification. Those drivers can be used by Microsoft for their new OS. They may or may not work, depending on what changes in the new OS.

Many Laptop makers don't expect people to install their own OS. The OEM (Original Equipment Manufacture) may include drivers and software that isn't part of the official Microsoft certification system. As such if you install the OS yourself, old or new, you may not have access to those drivers and software. The hardware that needs them wont work then.

In ether case most manufacturers won't update their drivers until the new OS is is finalized, or close to it. In the case of laptops that may be 4+ years old, they may never get updated. The OEMs again don't expect people to install the OS on their own. So don't feel they need to support the latest software on old hardware. Unless they want to give people install disks that contain their special drivers and software already. That is relatively rare though.

You can find out a lot about yourself and your ideas through disagreement. Sometimes those disagreements can get loud. I would not advocate poking at someone or 'stirring the pot' with the sole intent of causing chaos, but sometimes chaos arises naturally in a thread.

Disagreement is what makes a discussion healthy, but allowing discussions to consistently rise to the level of 'conflict' puts your forum into an unstable peak which, if not dealt with strictly, tend to devolve into one of two outcomes:

  1. the forum becomes a space where two opposing sides meet to shout at each other how wrong the other is, and where moderates must pick a side or be subjected to the attacks from either end, or

  2. one side gets large enough that they can wear down and intimidate those who don't agree, where the emotional effort required to participate for those dissenting users all but guarantees that the forum devolves into an echo chamber.

The only real way to keep a forum at that delicate equilibrium as it grows in size and attracts new members is to strictly enforce a high degree of civility, and remove comments that don't meet that standard. Not every forum really needs this, but if you want to keep interesting discussions happening and don't want an echo chamber, then that's precisely what you need.

A hands-off approach would be the most effective. Seeing as individual users have the ability to block specific users and avoid particular subverses, there shouldn't be any issues where a user is forced to view content they find undesirable. By having a completely open platform, people are able to pick and choose what they prefer. And if what they want isn't here? They have complete freedom to create it themselves.
